description: Live view over the TmChat composer, handed to the TmChat.ComposerTemplate render fragment. A host that fully replaces the built-in composer (subscribe gate, PPV field, owner note + hint, …) keeps the component's send path, submit state and draft guard working by driving its own input through this context: bind the input to Text, push each keystroke with SetTextAsync and send with SendAsync. Text is the source of truth — the template is re-rendered from it, so a controlled input bound to composer.Text clears itself after a send. The context is a live view over the owning TmChat, not a snapshot — every member reads the component's current state, so a context instance captured from an earlier render stays usable after the component re-renders.

members.name: Text
members.description: The current composer text as the component sees it — the source of truth the template is rendered from: what the built-in textarea holds, or whatever the custom composer last pushed through SetTextAsync. Bind a controlled input to it; empty again after SendAsync (the re-render propagates the cleared text into the bound input).

members.name: CanSend
members.description: Whether sending is currently allowed — the composer is not disabled, not already submitting and holds text that is not whitespace-only. Mirror it on a custom send button's disabled state; SendAsync ignores the request when it is false.

members.name: Disabled
members.description: Whether the component's Disabled parameter is set (a gate such as a closed subscription typically drives it).

members.name: IsSubmitting
members.description: Whether a send is currently in flight (the host handler has not completed yet). While it is true, CanSend is false and further SendAsync calls are ignored.

members.name: InputId
members.description: DOM id TmChat assigns to the built-in composer textarea, usable for a custom label (aria-describedby, label for) or aria-controls. The attribute is present in the DOM only while the built-in textarea actually renders — with a custom composer (or ShowComposer=false) there is no built-in textarea to point at. With TmChat.AutoAttachComposerInput, put this id on the ComposerTemplate input (id="@composer.InputId"); TmChat then attaches that element by id within its own root.

methods.name: SetTextAsync
methods.description: Pushes the text typed in a custom composer into the component, so the draft guard (HasUnsavedDraft / OnDraftChanged's HasComposerDraft) keeps covering a replaced composer exactly as it covers the built-in one. Call it from the custom input's oninput; does not trim — trimming happens on send.

methods.name: SendAsync
methods.description: Sends the current Text through the SAME path as the built-in send button: the text is trimmed and cleared, TmChat's OnSendMessage and OnSend fire, the submit state flips for the duration and the cleared composer is reported to the draft guard. A no-op when CanSend is false. The template re-renders with the cleared Text, so a controlled input clears itself after an awaited send. Safe to call from any thread — the send is dispatched onto the component's renderer synchronisation context.

methods.name: FocusAsync
methods.description: Moves focus to the composer input — the same logic as the post-send refocus: the element registered through AttachAsync if there is one, or the input auto-attached through TmChat.AutoAttachComposerInput, otherwise the built-in composer textarea. An element that already holds focus is left untouched (the module's focusIfNeeded), so a call from a host button does not close the on-screen keyboard. A best-effort no-op while nothing is focusable (no attached element with a custom composer, ShowComposer=false, or the circuit is gone).

examples:
<TmChat Messages="_messages" CurrentUser="_user" OnSend="@HandleSend">
    <ComposerTemplate Context="composer">
        <!-- controlled input: Text is the source of truth -->
        <textarea value="@composer.Text" disabled="@composer.Disabled"
                  @oninput="@(e => composer.SetTextAsync(e.Value?.ToString() ?? string.Empty))"></textarea>
        <button disabled="@(!composer.CanSend)" @onclick="composer.SendAsync">Send</button>
    </ComposerTemplate>
</TmChat>
